segments.title: HMS Africa remembered in song
segments.body: The song celebrates HMS Africa through a sailor's confidence that she will keep going. Its opening combines war drums with quiet conversation below decks, eight bells, and moonlight. The old 64-gun ship endures shot and shell in the refrain, which insists that she will arrive in time to do what she must. Calling Africa a goddess expresses affection and loyalty. The closing remarks recommend the Trafalgar videos for a fuller account of the ship.

evidence.note: The song repeatedly names HMS Africa, describes shell and shot falling on her, and identifies her as an old 64-gun ship.
Dr. Clarke describes HMS Africa as a very cool ship and directs viewers to the Trafalgar videos through a link below.

segments.summary: A musical tribute portrays HMS Africa as an old 64-gun ship enduring shot and shell, with a closing pointer to the Trafalgar videos.
